$comment: First-load budgets for the web app. Enforced by src/size-budget.test.ts; reported on
every PR by tools/report-size-budget.mjs. JSON carries no comments, so the reasoning
lives in `why` fields and in apps/web/src/size-budget.test.ts's header.
WHAT IS BUDGETED is the TOTAL first-load payload -- the page shell plus every engine
artifact a user downloads before their first operation can run -- not only per-file
sizes. Three files each growing 4% is a 4% regression that no 10%-per-file budget
notices. So `total` is the binding gate and the per-artifact lines say WHERE it went.
ORIGIN. docs/spikes/0001-wasm-engines.md measured the option-1 payload at 6,502,775
raw / 2,200,580 brotli, 82% of it PDFium, and ROADMAP item 11 records that as 'the
starting point, not a target'. The shipped build has since drifted above it: qpdf is
now built from source against our own vendored zlib and libjpeg-turbo (1,199,200 raw
against the spike's 917,305), the Rust module has grown from 15,266 to 43,072, and
the three glue files the spike listed separately now live inside one worker bundle.
The numbers below are a fresh measurement of what actually ships, not the spike's
table. pdfium.wasm's brotli size is unchanged from the spike to the byte.
TO CHANGE A BUDGET: re-measure, update `measured_brotli` AND `budget_brotli`, and say
why in the commit. An engine pin bump is the expected reason. Raising a budget to make
CI pass without knowing what grew is the thing this file exists to prevent.
HOW A RECORDING IS HELD TO THE BUILD IT DESCRIBES.
Each artifact records `measured_sha256` beside its sizes, and src/size-budget-drift.ts
turns that into a contradiction the tests can see: same bytes must mean the same
recorded numbers. Identical bytes with a different `measured_brotli` is a FALSE RECORD,
not drift, and there is no tolerance for it.
This exists because the obvious gates do not cover it. Live sizes are checked against
`budget_brotli`, and the recorded lines are checked against each other -- so a recording
that drifts CONSISTENTLY satisfies both. Measured: `engines/burrow-worker.js` was
recorded at 255,535 raw / 45,052 brotli and measured 256,255 / 45,288 on an UNCHANGED
checkout, 236 brotli bytes from a differently-built, gitignored
`bindings/burrow-wasm/pkg/`. Nothing failed. M1 PR A corrected the number; a corrected
number is not a control, because the next drift is silent in exactly the same way.
`not_byte_reproducible` is the one window this cannot close exactly, and it is declared
rather than implied: those artifacts legitimately differ per machine, so they get a
`drift_tolerance` bound instead of an equality. Every entry needs a reason. An artifact
whose bytes change WITHOUT being on that list fails -- an engine moving underneath us
should not be waved through as 'probably the toolchain'. Two of the three entries were
predicted; `engines/qpdf.wasm` was NOT, and got there by failing CI and naming itself,
which is the check working rather than the check being wrong.
THE PAGE IS NOT ON THAT LIST, DELIBERATELY, AND IT TOOK TWO GOES. The CSP names every
engine by its content-hashed URL (ADR 0014), so any engine rebuild changes index.html --
CI reported `qpdf.wasm` and `page` together for that one cause. Exempting `page` would
have meant not checking the line the design system lives on because of something
belonging to a different line.
So each artifact records TWO digests: the raw bytes, and the bytes with generated engine
hashes replaced by a fixed token. Three cases, distinguished rather than collapsed:
raw match              -> exact size equality. Nothing changed, so no tolerance.
normalised match only  -> only the quoted engine hashes differ. The artifact's own
content is unchanged, but its SIZE may wobble, because two
16-hex tokens do not compress identically. A tight absolute
bound (64 bytes), not a percentage: 2% of the page is 433
bytes and a real CSS regression could hide under that.
normalised differs     -> a real change. Must be on not_byte_reproducible or it fails.
The middle case exists because collapsing it into the first was a bug, and CI caught it:
the check reported `page: the bytes are IDENTICAL to the recording, but measured_brotli
says 21652 and the build is 21650`. The bytes were not identical. The message was the
part that was false, and a check that misdescribes what it found is worse than one that
finds nothing.
Shortening that list is the real fix and it means making `pkg/` reproducible, which is a
build change nobody has made yet.

why: Per-artifact headroom is loose (10%) because those lines are diagnostic: they say
which file moved. Total headroom is tight (3%, about 67 KB) because that line is the
gate. The asymmetry is deliberate and makes the total bind first in every case that
matters -- 10% of pdfium alone is 8.5% of the total, so a single artifact cannot
reach its own ceiling without the total having failed long before.
`page` is the exception and is recorded as such rather than left to look like 10%:
its budget is an ABSOLUTE 50 KiB, 58x its measurement. The reason is on that line.

engines/pdfium.wasm.why: 82% of the payload. Prebuilt, pdfium-binaries chromium/8044; changes only on an engine pin bump.

engines/qpdf.wasm.why: Built from source at the pinned version against our vendored zlib and libjpeg-turbo, so it moves with a pin bump or a build-flag change.

engines/burrow-worker.js.why: The one bundle: prelude, bridge, both Emscripten glue files, wasm-bindgen glue, worker main. This is the line our own worker code moves, so it is the one worth watching on an ordinary PR.

engines/burrow_wasm_bg.wasm.why: The Rust binding. Grows as operations land, which is expected -- a merge implementation should move this line and nothing else.

engines/control.txt.why: A fixed 78-byte literal fetched at init to prove an allowlisted request succeeds (ADR 0014). It has no reason to change; if it does, that is worth a question.

page.why: The entry page and every same-origin asset it references, pooled -- Vite splits and names those chunks at its own discretion, so a per-file budget here would fail on a rename. An ABSOLUTE budget (50 KiB), not a percentage. M1 PR A moved this line from 881 to 21,652 brotli, and almost all of it is one file: the self-hosted typeface, 18,524 of it. That is a deliberate payload decision, not drift -- apps/web/fonts.toml records what the face is and what the alternatives cost (brotli: 47,804 unsubsetted, 31,620 subsetted with the full weight axis, 18,524 with the axis clipped to the 400-700 the design uses). The font is only in this measurement because BaseLayout preloads it: tools/first-load.mjs scans the markup and does not follow url(...) inside CSS, so a face referenced only from @font-face would be a real download this budget could not see. src/styles/tokens.test.ts fails if any @font-face here has no matching preload. The absolute budget still has 29 KiB of room, which is what it is for: failing CI on editorial work teaches people to raise budgets without reading them.

total.why: The binding gate. Everything a user downloads before their first operation runs. M1 PR A spent 20,771 brotli bytes of the headroom on the design system and its typeface; a further 236 is the `burrow-worker.js` re-measurement described above, which predates this change and is not part of it. `budget_brotli` is deliberately UNCHANGED: the payload grew for a reason that is written down, and raising the ceiling to match would convert a gate into a record of whatever happened.

not_byte_reproducible.engines/burrow_wasm_bg.wasm: wasm-pack output. bindings/burrow-wasm/pkg/ is gitignored and rebuilt per machine, so the bytes depend on the local Rust and wasm-bindgen versions rather than on anything committed.
not_byte_reproducible.engines/burrow-worker.js: Concatenates pkg/burrow_wasm.js, so it inherits the line above. THIS IS THE ONE THAT DRIFTED: recorded at 45,052 brotli and measuring 45,288 on an unchanged checkout, 236 bytes from a differently-built pkg/, with nothing failing.
not_byte_reproducible.engines/qpdf.wasm: Built from source by engines/build-wasm.sh rather than fetched, and OBSERVED to differ between a local build and CI -- which is how it got onto this list: the check failed and named it. The cause is not established. emsdk is pinned (ADR 0004), so a reproducible Emscripten build is plausible and the usual culprit is absolute paths baked in by the compiler; nobody has looked. Until someone does, this is a bound rather than a claim. pdfium.wasm is NOT here: it is a prebuilt vendored artifact and its bytes match.
